name: Corinthian Pink
lede: Corinthian pink is a dusty, purplish pink that appears in color lists from 1912, long before it was a fashion word.

sections.title: A purplish pink
sections.body:
Paterson defines *Corinthian pink* as a purplish pink, and lists it among the pinks [1]. The earliest record in our sources is Ridgway's color atlas of 1912, and the name later turns up in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 and in Maerz and Paul [2]. Its closest named neighbor is [[puce]], at a CIEDE2000 distance of 7.9, and a Ridgway name, Pinkish Vinaceous, is a near-duplicate at 2.2 [2].

No book we hold says why Corinthian, so the origin of the name is undocumented [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Corinthian pink is rare but widespread. It appears in 76 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, and it is rarer than 52% of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color (69% of 42 paintings) [3]. It is over-represented in India, at 3.9 times the expected rate (22 of 721 paintings), and most of all in Rajput painting, at 8.1 times (10 of 97) [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
